issues.t: Excessive oil burning on the 2.0L turbo
issues.sym: The low-oil warning comes on between oil changes, you add a quart every 1,000 miles or so, and you may see bluish smoke from the exhaust.
issues.why: Piston rings on early 2.0L turbo engines let oil into the cylinders, where it burns. High crankcase pressure adds to it. Audi changed the design for later engines and a class-action settlement extended coverage on many cars.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and never let it run low, since low oil can wreck the timing chain and turbo. Ask an Audi dealer for an oil consumption test and whether any extended coverage still applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner failure on the 2.0L turbo
issues.sym: A rattle for a few seconds on cold start, then misfires, rough running, hard starting or stalling. If the chain jumps, the engine can be destroyed.
issues.why: The original timing chain tensioner wears early and lets the chain go slack. Audi revised the part several times and extended timing component coverage on 2010-2013 cars.
issues.next: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle. Have the tensioner checked and replaced with the updated part before the chain skips.

issues.t: Water pump and thermostat housing leaks
issues.sym: Coolant warning light, a low coolant tank, a sweet smell, drips under the front, weak heat, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The water pump and thermostat housing are plastic and crack or warp with age and heat. It is one of the most reported problems across every A5, S5 and RS5 generation.
issues.next: Top up only with the correct Audi coolant and get the leak found quickly. Stop driving if the engine overheats. Replacing the pump and thermostat housing together is common.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on the S5 supercharged V6
issues.sym: A rattle for one to three seconds at cold start, followed later by misfires, rough idle and a check engine light.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioners on the supercharged 3.0L V6 wear. The chains sit at the back of the engine, so the repair usually means taking the engine out.
issues.next: Have a cold-start rattle checked early. Ask the dealer about Audi's bulletin for the 3.0 TFSI tensioner.

issues.t: S tronic dual-clutch shifting problems on the S5
issues.sym: Harsh or jerky shifts, hesitation at low speed, slipping into neutral, missing gears or no reverse, sometimes with limp mode.
issues.why: The mechatronic unit that controls the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox fails on some supercharged S5 models. Low or old fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid level checked. Service the fluid and filter about every 40,000 miles to help prevent it.

issues.t: S5 crank pulley breaks apart
issues.sym: Squealing or slipping belts, a sudden loss of supercharger power, and the steering can get heavy.
issues.why: The two-piece crankshaft pulley on the supercharged V6 can separate, which throws or damages the drive belts.
issues.next: Stop driving if the belt comes off, since the water pump and steering assist may stop working. Replace the pulley with the updated part and inspect the belts.

issues.t: Rocker arm failure on early turbo V6 S5
issues.sym: A loud ticking from the engine, rough idle, and metal flakes found in the oil.
issues.why: A small number of early 3.0L turbo V6 engines had rocker arms fail and shed metal into the engine.
issues.next: Stop and have it checked if the engine ticks louder than usual. Repairs can require rebuilding the cylinder head.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on the intake valves
issues.sym: Misfires, a rough idle, hesitation, worse fuel economy, vibration at higher revs and a check engine light, usually after 50,000-60,000 miles.
issues.why: These direct-injection engines spray fuel straight into the cylinders, so nothing washes the backs of the intake valves and carbon builds up there.
issues.next: Have the intake valves cleaned (walnut blasting) when misfires appear, roughly every 60,000-100,000 miles.

issues.t: Crankcase vent (PCV) valve fails and causes leaks
issues.sym: A whistle or hiss from the engine, rough idle, misfires, strong suction at the oil cap, rising oil use, or an oil leak at the back of the engine.
issues.why: The plastic crankcase vent valve or breather hose cracks. That causes a vacuum leak and pressure that can push out the rear main seal.
issues.next: Replace the PCV valve or breather hose as soon as it whistles; it can prevent a rear main seal job.

issues.t: Fuel pump control module overheats
issues.sym: An EPC light, stalling or hesitation, a no-start, or a dead battery after sitting.
issues.why: The fuel pump control module can overheat and keep running the pump, which can also damage the pump.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing the module alone often fixes it; the pump may also need replacing.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate rattle and low boost
issues.sym: Turbo lag, a rattle from the turbo area, a check engine light for underboost, or limp mode.
issues.why: The wastegate rod on the turbo can wear loose and leak boost. A bad boost control valve or diverter valve can cause similar symptoms.
issues.next: Have a smoke or boost test done to find the leak. A new valve sometimes fixes it; a worn wastegate usually means a new turbo.

issues.t: Oil consumption on the newer 2.0L turbo
issues.sym: You need to add oil between services, and the low-oil warning may come on.
issues.why: Some second-generation 2.0L turbo engines burn oil from piston ring wear, cylinder glazing or valve seal wear, usually noticed around 40,000-80,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the oil every few fill-ups. If it keeps dropping, ask a dealer for an oil consumption test while the car is under any warranty.

issues.t: Front control arm bushings wear out
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, creaks when turning, vibration in the steering wheel, vague steering and uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings and ball joints in the front control arms wear and crack early on Audis of this family.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Worn arms are often replaced in pairs, followed by an alignment.

issues.t: Sunroof creaks and rattles
issues.sym: Squeaks, creaks and popping from the sunroof over bumps, driveway ramps or turns.
issues.why: The body flexes slightly and parts of the sunroof frame rub together. Over time the frame can crack.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to pad and re-tighten the frame under warranty. Keep the sunroof drains clear too.

issues.t: Power window stops working or drops
issues.sym: A window sticks, moves slowly, makes crunching noises, or the motor runs without moving the glass. Frameless windows may not drop and rise properly when the door opens.
issues.why: The window motor or regulator wears out from constant use. A door module, fuse or wiring fault can do the same.
issues.next: Try the window reset (hold the switch down then up for 10 seconds each). If that fails, replace the motor or regulator.

issues.t: Outside door handle won't open the door
issues.sym: The outside handle feels loose or does nothing, so the door won't open from outside.
issues.why: The cable that links the handle to the latch sticks or stretches.
issues.next: Lubricating the cable often fixes it. If not, the cable can be replaced.

issues.t: MMI screen freezes or virtual cockpit glitches
issues.sym: The MMI screen freezes, reboots or starts slowly, or the digital instrument cluster shows blank patches.
issues.why: Software faults in the infotainment and display units, more common on cars built before the 2020 update.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the latest software. A reset often fixes it without new parts.

issues.t: Electric coolant pump can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Possible burning smell or overheating warning, but often no warning at all.
issues.why: Debris can jam the small electric coolant pump on the 2.0L turbo, or moisture can short it out, causing it to overheat. Audi first updated software, then replaced the pumps.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 17V-002 and 18V-229. The fix is free at an Audi dealer.

issues.t: Auxiliary heater wiring can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or melted wiring near the auxiliary heater.
issues.why: A connector on the auxiliary heater can corrode, overheat and melt its wires, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 17V-622. The dealer replaces the heater free.

issues.t: Airbag control unit can corrode and fail (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on, or there may be no sign until a crash.
issues.why: Moisture can corrode the airbag control unit so the airbags may not deploy.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-376. The dealer replaces the control unit free.

issues.t: Cabriolet driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: Takata driver airbag inflators in A5 and S5 Cabriolets can rupture when they deploy and throw metal fragments.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall right away and get the inflator replaced free.

issues.t: S5 fuel rail can leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The fuel rails and seals on the 3.0L supercharged V6 can leak fuel, which could catch fire.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell fuel and check your VIN for recall 15V-019. The dealer replaces the rails and seals free.

issues.t: Cabriolet seat belt pretensioner part can break loose (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: A part in the seat belt pretensioners on 2017 A5 and S5 Cabriolets can come loose when it fires and fly through the cabin.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the retractors free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may switch itself off (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light comes on with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A faulty seat heater cable or corroded occupant-detection wiring can make the system think the seat is empty and turn off the passenger airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 19V-547 and 21V-874. The dealer repairs the wiring and seat heater free.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may not unfold properly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The head curtain airbags on some 2018 A5 Coupes may not unfold correctly to help keep occupants inside in a rollover.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 17V-822. The dealer modifies the airbags free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag mounting screw may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: A screw holding the passenger airbag module may not have been tightened enough, which could affect how it deploys.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-836. The dealer tightens or replaces the screw free.

issues.t: Front suspension bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front or a change in steering feel.
issues.why: Some front suspension fasteners were not tightened enough at the factory, which could let a front wheel come loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-893. The dealer inspects and replaces the fasteners free.

issues.t: Door speaker trim can leave sharp edges (recall)
issues.sym: The aluminum trim around a door speaker comes loose and exposes a sharp edge.
issues.why: The speaker trim was not attached securely on some 2018 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 17V-675. The dealer replaces the speaker covers free.

issues.t: S5 front shock absorber forks can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the front suspension or a change in handling.
issues.why: The forks that hold the front shock absorbers can crack and let the shocks come loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-114. The dealer replaces the forks free.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm nut can crack (recall)
issues.sym: The car may pull, handle oddly or wear the rear tires unevenly.
issues.why: A lock nut on the rear trailing arm can crack from stress corrosion and throw the rear wheel out of line. A follow-up recall added an alignment check that was missed the first time.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 21V-295 and 22V-034. The dealer replaces the nuts, aligns the rear axle and replaces worn tires free.

issues.t: Taillight wiring can chafe through (recall)
issues.sym: A rear light fault warning or a taillight that stops working.
issues.why: Wiring for the rear lights near the spare wheel well was missing a protective sleeve and can wear through.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-737. The dealer adds protection free.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: A rear belt doesn't stay locked when you install a child seat.
issues.why: The automatic locking feature in some rear belt retractors can switch off too early.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-606. Use LATCH anchors for the child seat until it is fixed.

issues.t: Rearview camera shows a blank screen (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the screen stays black or blank instead of showing the camera.
issues.why: Infotainment software errors, and on some 2022 cars internal damage to the main unit at shut-off, can stop the camera image from showing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 22V-742, 21V-825 and 22V-806. The dealer updates the software or replaces the unit free.

issues.t: S5 passenger airbag may be turned off (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light comes on with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A loose connection in the passenger seat occupant detection module can switch off the front passenger airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-251. The dealer replaces the module free.
